question: What will be the percentage change in front-month silver futures (SI=F on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-08-14 to the close on 2026-09-20?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-09-20 / close on 2026-08-14 - 1), using daily closes of SI=F on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-09-20, the last close before it is used.

from the empirical distribution of 25-observation returns over the last 3 years (last year weighted double):

research:
I'm writing up the brief now, using only sources dated on or before 2026-08-16. Many search results were dated later than that, so I left them out.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-14: Yahoo Finance's SI=F closed at **64.988**. That is the base value from the data collected by code. I could not open Yahoo directly to check it.
- 2026-08-14: A secondary source gave spot silver at about $63.98 that morning, down 1.56% from the prior close of $64.99. September futures traded between $63.85 and $64.88 during the session. [naturalresourcestocks](https://naturalresourcestocks.net/silver-price-today-aug-14-2026/)
- Note on the contract: SI=F follows the front-month COMEX contract. The September 2026 contract (SIU26) reaches first notice around late August, so Yahoo's series probably switches to December (SIZ26) before 2026-09-20. December usually trades a little above September (contango, maybe about 0.5% to 1%). That switch could add a small upward jump to the measured change. I have not confirmed the exact switch date.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. The 25-session window runs from 2026-08-14 to 2026-09-18.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-14: Silver pulled back after rising above $66 earlier in the week. [naturalresourcestocks](https://naturalresourcestocks.net/silver-price-today-aug-14-2026/)
- 2026-08-12: Silver was near $64.78 after trading between 64.23 and 66.49, with traders waiting for CPI. [ISA Bullion](https://www.isabullion.com/?p=8607)
- About 2026-08-12/13: July CPI came in soft, up 0.1% for the month, with the annual rate easing to 3.4% from 3.5%. Market odds of a September Fed **hike** fell to about one-third, which supported metals. [FXEmpire](https://www.fxempire.com/forecasts/article/gold-xau-usd-silver-price-forecast-softer-cpi-shifts-focus-to-ppi-whats-next-1616519)
- 2026-08-10: Silver opened CPI week flat near $63.50, close to a roughly seven-week high of $65.16 set on 08-07. The July jobs report was weak (reportedly -23K against +80K expected), and CME FedWatch odds of a September hike fell to 46% from 67%. [TMGM/FXStreet](https://www.tmgm.com/es/analysis/market-news/article/silver-price-forecast-xag-usd-starts-us-cpi-week-on-flat-note-around-6350-202608100316)
- Background: the Fed under Chair Warsh is weighing **rate hikes** with inflation around 3.4%. That works against non-yielding metals, so silver is very sensitive to how hike odds move.

## 4. Base rates
- From the code's empirical distribution of 25-session returns over the last 3 years (last year weighted double), expressed as % change from 64.988:
  - p5: -18.1%
  - p10: -11.6%
  - p25: -3.4%
  - p50: +3.3%
  - p75: +10.5%
  - p90: +20.6%
  - p95: +34.2%
- This is a very wide range. Silver has been extremely volatile over 2025-26, and that history includes the big rally and crash. The middle 50% of outcomes spans about 14 percentage points.
- July 2026 monthly high (based on daily highs) was about $62.62, per a Manifold question. Silver went from the low $60s in July to $63-66 in early-to-mid August, about seven-week highs. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/uair01/silver-futures-price-august-2026-be)

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi and Robinhood list daily and hourly silver-price contracts. I did not find a market price as of 2026-08-16 for a mid or late September level. [Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/us/en/prediction-markets/metals/events/silver-price-august-6-2026-aug-06-2026/)
- I did not find any bank forecasts made before the cutoff that target mid-September.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Week of 08-17: FOMC minutes (from the July meeting).
- Late August (about 08-27 to 08-29): Jackson Hole symposium, where a Warsh speech would be a key signal on hikes.
- About 08-27/28: first notice for the September COMEX contract and the likely SI=F switch to December.
- 2026-09-04: August jobs report.
- About 2026-09-10/11: August CPI and PPI.
- FOMC meeting in mid-September, scheduled before the resolution date (about 09-15/16). Whether the Fed hikes is the biggest single risk.
- Ongoing: moves in the US dollar and Treasury yields, Middle East geopolitics, and the structural silver supply deficit.
